Complex structure (J)

Words: 11k Articles: 273
Complex geometry OurBigBook.com
A complex structure on a real vector space or vector bundle is an endomorphism J satisfying J2=−I. On a smooth manifold, an integrable complex structure determines holomorphic coordinate charts.

Space of orthogonal complex structures (O(2n)/U(n))

Words: 48
Complex structure OurBigBook.com
On a Euclidean real space of dimension 2n, an orthogonal complex structure is an orthogonal endomorphism J with J2=−I. Orthogonal changes of basis act transitively on these structures, and the stabilizer of the standard structure is U(n). The compact homogeneous space has real dimension n(n−1).

Almost complex manifold

Words: 11k Articles: 271
Complex structure OurBigBook.com
An almost complex manifold is a smooth manifold X with a bundle endomorphism J:TX→TX satisfying J2=−I.

Almost complex structure from a decomposable volume form (JΩ​)

Words: 128 Articles: 1
Almost complex manifold OurBigBook.com
A locally decomposable complex n-form Ω on a real 2n-manifold, with Ω∧Ω nowhere zero, determines an almost complex structure. The intrinsic rank-n subbundle W={α∈T∗M⊗C:α∧Ω=0} is locally spanned by the factors of Ω. The nonvanishing condition gives T∗M⊗C=W⊕W. Set J∗=i on W and J∗=−i on W. This commutes with conjugation, so comes from a unique real bundle endomorphism with square −I.
Closed decomposable complex volume forms are integrable
Words: 58
Almost complex structure from a decomposable volume form OurBigBook.com
If Ω=θ1​∧⋯∧θn​ and dΩ=0, differentiating θj​∧Ω=0 gives dθj​∧Ω=0. Only the (0,2) component of dθj​ can survive this wedge product; multiplication by Ω is injective on that component. Thus no dθj​ has a (0,2) part. The bracket and differential-form criteria for integrability make the induced almost complex structure integrable. Local decomposability is part of the hypothesis and is not implied solely by nonvanishing of Ω∧Ω.

Type decomposition of the complexified tangent bundle (TC​X=T1,0X⊕T0,1X)

Words: 27
Almost complex manifold OurBigBook.com
An almost complex structure J gives the +i and −i eigenbundles of its complex-linear extension. Their projections are (I−iJ)/2 and (I+iJ)/2. For an integrable structure the first is the holomorphic tangent bundle.

Totally real submanifold

Words: 38
Almost complex manifold OurBigBook.com
In the maximal-dimension convention, a totally real submanifold of (M,J) has half the real dimension of M and Tp​L∩J(Tp​L)=0. Every Lagrangian submanifold is totally real for a compatible almost complex structure, but the converse fails in complex dimension at least two.

Compatible almost complex structure (J)

Words: 169 Articles: 4
Almost complex manifold OurBigBook.com
An almost complex structure J on a symplectic manifold (M,ω) is compatible with ω when
ω(Ju,Jv)=ω(u,v)
(1)
and gJ​(u,v)=ω(u,Jv) is a positive-definite inner product. Every symplectic vector bundle admits a compatible almost complex structure.
Contractibility of compatible almost complex structures
Words: 37
Compatible almost complex structure OurBigBook.com
The metric construction of a compatible almost complex structure is continuous in the auxiliary Riemannian metric, and recovers J when applied to gJ​=ω(⋅,J⋅). Interpolating gJ​ linearly to a fixed auxiliary metric therefore contracts the space of compatible almost complex structures. In particular it is nonempty and path connected.
Compatible triple ((ω,J,g))
Words: 16
Compatible almost complex structure OurBigBook.com
A compatible triple consists of a symplectic form, a compatible almost complex structure, and the Riemannian metric g(u,v)=ω(u,Jv). Equivalently g(Ju,v)=ω(u,v).
Metric construction of a compatible almost complex structure
Words: 38
Compatible almost complex structure OurBigBook.com
Choose an auxiliary Riemannian metric h and define the skew-adjoint bundle map A by ω(u,v)=h(Au,v). Then
J=A(−A2)−1/2
(2)
is a compatible almost complex structure. The positive square root is defined fiberwise by the spectral theorem for normal operators, and its smooth dependence on A makes J smooth.
Relative extension of a compatible almost complex structure
Words: 51
Compatible almost complex structure OurBigBook.com
If a compatible almost complex structure is prescribed along a closed symplectic submanifold N⊂M and preserves TN, it extends to one on M. Choose a compatible structure separately on TN and its symplectic normal bundle, use the associated metric along N, extend that metric to M, and apply the metric construction of a compatible almost complex structure.

Nijenhuis tensor (NJ​)

Words: 22
Almost complex manifold OurBigBook.com
The Nijenhuis tensor of an almost complex manifold is
NJ​(U,V)=[JU,JV]−J[JU,V]−J[U,JV]−[U,V].
(3)
It measures the failure of the (0,1) tangent distribution to be closed under the Lie bracket.

Integrable almost complex structure

Words: 11k Articles: 260
Almost complex manifold OurBigBook.com
An almost complex structure is integrable when it comes from holomorphic coordinate charts. Equivalently, its Nijenhuis tensor vanishes, or the (0,1) vector fields are closed under Lie bracket.
Bracket and differential-form criteria for integrability
Words: 57
Integrable almost complex structure OurBigBook.com
For an almost complex structure, closure of T1,0 under the Lie bracket is equivalent to the absence of a (0,2) component in dα for every (1,0)-form α. Conjugation exchanges the bracket condition with closure of T0,1. For sections U,V of T0,1, the exterior derivative identity gives dα(U,V)=−α([U,V]). Its vanishing for all (1,0)-forms is exactly [U,V]∈T0,1.
Newlander-Nirenberg theorem
Words: 15
Integrable almost complex structure OurBigBook.com
The Newlander-Nirenberg theorem says that a smooth almost complex structure is integrable if and only if its Nijenhuis tensor vanishes.
Complex manifold
Words: 11k Articles: 257
Integrable almost complex structure OurBigBook.com
A complex n-manifold has charts to Cn with holomorphic transition maps. It is a real 2n-manifold with an integrable almost complex structure.
Holomorphic map between complex manifolds (F:M⟶N)
Words: 57
Complex manifold OurBigBook.com
A map between complex manifolds is holomorphic when its local coordinate expression has holomorphic scalar components. For a smooth map, this is equivalent to its differential being complex-linear at every point. These maps compose by the chain rule. For one-dimensional manifolds this reduces to a holomorphic map between Riemann surfaces; the general definition also applies to multiplication and inversion on a complex Lie group.
Smooth proper family of compact complex manifolds (f:X→S)
Words: 44
Complex manifold OurBigBook.com
A proper holomorphic submersion has compact smooth fibres, and the Ehresmann fibration theorem gives differentiable local trivializations. Their integral cohomology, modulo torsion, forms a local system. If the fibres are Kähler manifolds, their Hodge filtrations form holomorphic subbundles and give a variation of Hodge structure. Properness is needed for this usual conclusion.
Irreducible analytic subvariety of a complex manifold
Words: 58
Complex manifold OurBigBook.com
An analytic subvariety is a closed subset locally defined by finitely many holomorphic functions. It is irreducible if it is not the union of two proper closed analytic subsets. An irreducible analytic subvariety of complex codimension k in an n-dimensional complex manifold has pure complex dimension n−k. Global irreducibility does not forbid multiple local branches at a singular point.
Complex surface (dimC​M=2)
Words: 683 Articles: 13
Complex manifold OurBigBook.com
A complex surface is a complex manifold of complex dimension two, hence real dimension four. Compact complex surfaces need not admit a Kähler metric; a Hopf surface is an example. Every holomorphic one-form on a compact complex surface is closed, and the Betti and Hodge bounds for compact complex surfaces still apply without Kähler assumptions.
K3 surface
Words: 643 Articles: 12
Complex surface OurBigBook.com
A complex K3 surface is a compact, simply connected complex surface with trivial canonical bundle. For projective algebraic surfaces, one can equivalently require a trivial canonical bundle and H1(X,OX​)=0. Nonprojective complex K3 surfaces are also included, which is essential for the full moduli space of Ricci-flat K3 metrics.
Fermat quartic surface (x04​+x14​+x24​+x34​=0)
Words: 69
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
Over C, the four partial derivatives show that this projective surface is smooth. Adjunction makes its canonical bundle trivial, and the hypersurface exact sequence gives H1(OX​)=0, so it is a K3 surface. Lines given by x0​=ζx1​, x2​=ηx3​, with ζ4=η4=−1, lie on it. Choosing both roots differently gives skew lines, one of which is a section of the elliptic pencil defined by planes through the other.
Global Torelli theorem for K3 surfaces (ϕ=f∗:H2(Y,Z)→H2(X,Z))
Words: 50
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
An integral Hodge isometry between complex K3 surfaces which carries some Kähler class to a Kähler class is the pullback of a unique isomorphism of the surfaces. A Hodge isometry without that cone condition need not itself be geometric: reflection in an effective (−2)-curve reverses its class and cannot be induced by an isomorphism.
K3 linear system dichotomies
Words: 67
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
For nef big systems on a complex K3 surface, the successive alternatives distinguish a monogonal linear system on a K3 surface from a basepoint-free system; then a degree-two map from a birational map; then a projective ideal generated by quadrics from the trigonal and plane-quintic exceptions. The last alternatives must include the low-genus quartic and quadric-cubic models. The birational morphism can contract exactly the orthogonal (−2)-curves; it need not embed the original smooth surface.
Trigonal linear system on a K3 surface (D⋅E=3)
Words: 49
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
For a basepoint-free nonhyperelliptic nef big divisor D, the trigonal condition means that its general smooth curve is a trigonal curve. An elliptic pencil on a K3 surface with D⋅E=3 restricts to its degree-three pencil. On a smooth quartic containing a line Γ, the hyperplane class H has this property for E=H−Γ.
Hyperelliptic linear system on a K3 surface (degφ∣D∣​=2)
Words: 53
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
For a basepoint-free nef big divisor D, this means that the morphism given by its complete system is generically two-to-one onto its image. Equivalently, its general smooth curve is hyperelliptic. A double cover of P2 branched over a smooth sextic, with the pullback of O(1), gives the degree-two example.
Elliptic pencil on a K3 surface (E2=0,∣E∣≅P1)
Words: 85 Articles: 1
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
A primitive effective nef class of square zero on a complex K3 surface defines a basepoint-free pencil with connected genus-one fibres. Its general fibre is a smooth elliptic curve. A section is a smooth rational curve Γ with E⋅Γ=1 and Γ2=−2.
Monogonal linear system on a K3 surface (D=mE+Γ,m≥2)
Words: 49
Elliptic pencil on a K3 surface OurBigBook.com
For a nef big divisor, the monogonal case is the fixed-section system ∣D∣=Γ+∣mE∣, where E is an elliptic pencil on a K3 surface and Γ is a section. Thus D⋅E=1. The fixed part persists even though D is nef; the general divisor is reducible. Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic surfaces gives h0(D)=m+1=h0(mE), proving the equality of systems.
Moduli space of Ricci-flat K3 metrics (SO(3,19)/(SO(3)×SO(19))×R>0​)
Words: 55
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
Locally, a unit-volume Ricci flat metric on a K3 surface determines a positive three-plane in its real second cohomology, with the K3 intersection lattice fixed. The corresponding Grassmannian has dimension 3⋅19=57. Allowing the volume gives one further positive real parameter; large diffeomorphisms identify lattice-equivalent descriptions. This is the same continuous moduli count as the three-torus Narain moduli space plus its coupling.

Fixed-part elimination on a K3 surface
Words: 68
K3 surface OurBigBook.com
If D is a nontrivial nef divisor on a K3 surface with D2=0, its complete linear system of a divisor has no fixed part. Write D=F+M. Nefness of D and M gives D⋅F=D⋅M=M2=M⋅F=F2=0. But a nonzero fixed part satisfies h0(F)=1, while Riemann–Roch theorem for algebraic surfaces and Serre duality would give h0(F)≥2 if F2=0. Hence F=0. Two movable members with no common component have intersection zero and are disjoint, so the system is basepoint-free and has Iitaka dimension one.

Complex manifold OurBigBook.com
A complex manifold is Stein if its global holomorphic functions separate points, give local coordinates, and make it holomorphically convex: the holomorphic hull of every compact set is compact. Closed complex submanifolds of affine complex space are examples, including products of copies of C and C∗. Cartan theorem B makes these spaces useful for acyclic covers in sheaf cohomology.

Complex submanifold OurBigBook.com
Let Y be a embedded submanifold of a complex manifold. If its tangent spaces are invariant under the almost complex structure induced by a complex atlas, choose ambient holomorphic coordinates making its tangent space at one point Ck×0. Invariance of the tangent graph gives dF(iv)=idF(v), the Cauchy-Riemann equations. Thus F is holomorphic and these graph coordinates give the induced complex submanifold structure. This proves the result directly, without needing the general integrability theorem as an unproved step.

Local defining function of a complex analytic hypersurface OurBigBook.com
The local ring of a complex manifold is the unique factorization domain of convergent power series in local coordinates. A reduced local defining function of a complex analytic hypersurface has each local irreducible factor once. The analytic zero-set ideal is the radical of its principal ideal, and reducedness makes that principal ideal radical. Thus two reduced equations for the same germ generate the same ideal and differ by a unit. A globally irreducible hypersurface may have several local branches; reducedness includes each once. Without reducedness, f and f2 have the same zero set and need not differ by a unit.

If a holomorphic class equals an antiholomorphic class, their difference is df, and ∂∂ˉf=0; compact pluriharmonic rigidity makes both forms vanish. Their direct sum gives the lower bound. The sheaf of closed holomorphic one-forms exact sequence gives 0→H0(Ω1)→H1(C)→H1(O), yielding the upper bound and h1,0≤h0,1. These inequalities do not require a Kähler manifold.

Chern connection OurBigBook.com
For a Hermitian metric on a complex manifold, the Chern connection on its holomorphic tangent bundle corresponds to a real metric-compatible connection preserving the almost complex structure. Its mixed torsion vanishes, and in holomorphic coordinates its remaining coefficients are Γijk​=hklˉ∂i​hjlˉ​. Symmetry in i,j is equivalent to ∂ω=0; its conjugate gives dω=0. Thus zero torsion is exactly the Kähler metric condition, and then uniqueness identifies this connection with the Levi-Civita connection.

Chern connection OurBigBook.com
The vector-bundle curvature of the unique metric-compatible holomorphic Chern connection is an endomorphism-valued form of type (1,1). It is Dolbeault closed and represents the curvature Dolbeault class. Its trace gives normalized first-Chern forms, while its full endomorphism action enters the Lefschetz-Dolbeault curvature commutator.

In a holomorphic local frame, a Hermitian metric on a holomorphic vector bundle has matrix h. The trace of its Chern connection curvature is ∂ˉ∂logdeth. The blowup replaces a point of a complex n-manifold by the projective space of complex tangent directions CPn−1. A biholomorphism carrying one center to another lifts to a biholomorphism of their blowups.
It is the point-center case of blowup of an algebraic variety, also interpreted analytically.
